newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Immobel buys disputed Brussels green area.
newsitem.headline: Immobel buys disputed Brussels green area.

text.p: Belgian real estate group Immobel SA bought a disputed green patch of land in the Brussels European Union district for 200 million francs from the Belgian state at a public auction on Tuesday.

Immobel managing director Jean Thomas told Reuters after the sale that he hoped his company would be able to develop an office complex at the site, which is located between Rue de la Loi, Chaussee d'Etterbeek, Rue Taciturne and Rue Joseph II.
A building permit request by Immobel unit Egimmo has been rejected by the city council following protest by neighbours.
"This is one of the few green areas in the EU area. It should remain a park," said Grace Faes, one of the area's residents who handed out protest leaflets at the auction.
A Belgian Finance Ministry official said the 6,200 square metre was originally meant for office construction.
The Brussels City Council at its September 12 meeting rejected the building permit request, arguing that the plot should remain a park.
Thomas said that the council decision had not yet been notified to Egimmo and that he would appeal it when it comes.
Part of the plot is rented to the European Union as a parking lot for 767,000 francs per year. The rest is made up of a small triangular park.
